status.description: Exit conclusion. `needs_iteration` alone means a check ran and disagreed with the source. The others mean nothing contradicted the breakdown, and report how far the evidence reached: `verified` (structure and scalars both bound to the capture), `verified_unbound_scalars` (structure verified against source, scalars resting on unbound defaults), `structure_unverified` (no source to check topology against), `exploratory` (too little evidence for the score to carry weight). `passed` is the pre-tier spelling, retained so older reports still validate. `passed_at_cap` means the breakdown met the quality bar for the evidence supplied: quality_rate at or above minimum_quality_rate, every core dimension passing, and all hard gates clear, at an evidence_cap that may be below 100. It is a full pass, not a partial one -- the cap describes the inputs, not the work.

convertible.description: Whether this conclusion may be turned into a UI report.

tier_ceiling.description: Strongest conclusion the evidence supports, after capability promotions.

nominal_tier_ceiling.description: Ceiling from the tier alone, before promotions.

runnable_max.description: Total weight of checks that had evidence to run against.

nominal_max.description: Total weight if every input were supplied.

correctness_ratio.description: score / runnable_max: correctness among what could be checked.

evidence_fraction.description: runnable_max / nominal_max: how much of the nominal check set had evidence.

status.description: `unevaluated` means no component in this dimension had evidence to run against, so it proved nothing. It is not a pass: a 0/0 ratio would be a vacuous 1.0.

skipped_weights.description: Components excluded from the denominator because their evidence was never supplied. Every entry has to be justified by a missing input; skipping a runnable check to raise the ratio is forbidden by the report's own constraints.

quality_rate.description: Correctness among currently checkable items, 0-1. This is what the pass gate reads; final_score is never gated on.

evidence_cap.description: Highest score the supplied inputs permit, from the fixed table in references/breakdown_scoring.md. Depends only on which of source / checkpoint config / trace are present, never on how well the breakdown scored. A Python default in modeling source is NOT a bound checkpoint config.

final_score.description: quality_rate x evidence_cap. Descriptive only: MUST NOT be used as a pass threshold, which is why the old final_score >= 95 gate is gone.

minimum_quality_rate.description: The quality_rate bar for a formal pass (0.95).

passed_at_cap.description: The only formal downstream gate. True only when quality_rate and every required dimension pass, deterministic hard gates are clear, and a digest-bound, deterministically validated independent critique clears the candidate.

evidence_cap_detail.description: Which of source / checkpoint config / trace were detected, and the resulting cap with its reason.

critique_cleared.description: A bound critique report cleared this candidate: no error issues, all eleven checks passed, digests current. Required for passed_at_cap.

critique_gates.description: Hard gates derived from the independent final critique.
